correctness.rationale: A labeled 30-edge host graph and exact shortest-path matrix reconstruct all 66 two-vertex equidistance classes, rule out 1- and 2-landmark resolving sets, and characterize the 160 resolving triples. Every candidate triple among \(\binom{12}{3}=220\) is checked; every single replacement is checked to build the complete 160-state graphs. Two independent standard-library integer programs enumerate all source BFS rows and all 12720 pair distances, verify eccentricity distribution and transport comparisons using six bijections. The Python checker independently compares the transport baseline against shortest paths in the full 220-state token graph. Graph-invariant checks, bounds and source code are embedded; no statistical or infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The family contains every optimal graph-metric landmark set on a canonical symmetric host. Its antipodal-partition-matroid description explains full membership structurally and motivates comparing freely exchanged bases to locally movable landmark sensors. The result gives the entire constrained reconfiguration graph's exact distance spectrum and sharp diameter and quantifies a genuine obstruction: 610 and only 610 of 12720 pairs need one move beyond the unconstrained transport distance. This is an exact natural finite metric classification, not a routine numerical restatement of the known metric dimension.
